articles.title: Nigerian stock market valuation hits all-time high of N162.39 trillion - 21st CENTURY CHRONICLE

articles.full_text:
The Nigerian Exchange (NGX) market capitalisation rose to an all-time high on Monday after closing at N162.39 trillion.
NGX valuation rose by 0.14 per cent from the N162.15 trillion recorded on Friday.
This followed a 352.24 basis points increase in the all-share index (ASI), which closed at 250,156.80 ASI, above Friday’s 249,804.56 index.
On Monday, trading ended with 68,655 deals involving 574.19 million shares valued at N38.06 billion.
The highest trading volume was recorded by Zenith Bank with 77.07 million shares valued at N9.90 billion, followed by Mutual Benefits Assurance with 53.58 million shares worth N205.59 million, and Sterling Financial Holdings with 44.23 million shares valued at N339.33 million.
Guaranty Trust Holding Company (GTCO) traded 25.86 million shares valued at N3.41 billion, while AIICO Insurance recorded 24.38 million shares worth N91.92 million.
Omatek Industrie led the gainers, rising by 10 per cent from N1.20 to N1.32.
Thomas Wyatt Nigeria also gained 10 per cent, moving from N2.30 to N2.53, while NASCON Allied Industries rose by 10 per cent from N160 to N176.
SUNU Assurances increased by 10 per cent from N2.80 to N3.08, while Consolidated Merchant Bank gained 9.8 per cent, rising from N2.04 to N2.24.
Okomu Oil Palm led the decliners, falling by 10 per cent from N1,418 to N1,276.20.
Custodian Investment declined by 9.13 per cent from N75 to N68.15, while Sovereign Trust Insurance fell by 8.64 per cent from N2.20 to N2.01.
Haldane McCall dropped by 8.33 per cent from N3.60 to N3.30, while Ellah Lakes declined by 5.39 per cent from N8.35 to N7.90.

articles.title: Despite yellow alert, Goa swelters under ‘feels like’ temperature of 41°C - The Times of India

articles.full_text:
Panaji: Despite the India Meteorological Department’s (IMD) yellow alert rainfall warning for the day, maximum temperatures across the state remained uncomfortably elevated at 2°C above normal levels. Official weather observations revealed that completely dry conditions prevailed across Goa on Tuesday, with meteorological stations registering zero precipitation over the last 24-hour cycle. In Panaji, actual temperatures hovered around 31.6°C, but high humidity levels near 75% spiked the apparent temperature index to 41°C, matching the scorching heat index of 41.9°C recorded in the desert of Bikaner, Rajasthan, the same day.
The IMD, which had initially issued a three-day yellow alert from Sept 22 to 24, reduced the alert to only two days on Tuesday. The IMD has warned of a thunderstorm accompanied by lightning and gusty winds (30-40kmph), with heavy rainfall likely to occur at isolated places over North and South Goa on Wednesday.
Cumulative seasonal totals indicate an average rainfall deficit of 32.5% for Goa, with North Goa trailing normal figures by 37% and South Goa down by 28.4% since the start of the monsoon cycle.
As persistent atmospheric dry spells continue to overwrite rain forecasts, the contrast between official weather warnings and ground-level reality highlights growing weather volatility, leaving the region sweltering without immediate environmental respite.
The prolonged dry spell has deepened the state’s cumulative seasonal deficit. Since June 1, Goa has recorded 1,981.7mm of rainfall against a seasonal normal of 2,937mm, representing an overall shortfall of 32.5%. North Goa remains the hardest hit with a 37% deficit, while South Goa trails normal levels by 28.4%. Despite a yellow alert, Goa swelters under a “feels like” temperature of 41°C, hotter than Bikaner.

The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued red alert for extremely heavy rainfall over isolated places of Chhattisgarh, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Telangana for the next two days. The Met Department has predicted heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Bihar, Jharkhand, Kerala, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. The weather department also forecast thunderstorms accompanied with highly gusty winds over Madhya Pradesh and Parts of North-East tomorrow.
For Delhi, IMD said the national capital will witness mostly clear skies with no rain. The maximum temperature in Delhi is expected to be around 34 to 35 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature of 23 to 25 degrees Celsius.

Hyderabad, Sep 22 (PTI) The IMD on Tuesday said very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall is very likely to occur at isolated places in Peddapalli, Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Mulugu and other districts of Telangana on September 23 and 24.
In its weather warnings, the Met Centre of IMD here also said heavy to very heavy rainfall is very likely to occur at isolated places in Komaram Bheem Asifabad, Mancherial, Jagtial, Karimnagar and other districts on Wednesday.
On September 24, heavy to very heavy rainfall is very likely to occur at isolated places in Adilabad, Nizamabad, Jagtial, Khammam and Nalgonda districts, it said in a release.
In view of the forecast of heavy rains, Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy instructed the Commissioners of Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation, Cyberabad Municipal Corporation and Malkajgiri Municipal Corporation, police commissioners and the Commissioner of Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA) to work in coordination and monitor the situation constantly.
The authorities were directed to take immediate measures to prevent water logging on main roads, junctions and residential colonies, besides other rain-relief measures, an official release said. PTI SJR SJR SA
